rules.title: San Francisco Rent Ordinance Just Cause Eviction Protections
rules.requirement: A landlord may only evict a tenant from a covered rental unit for one of 17 specific just cause reasons listed in the Rent Ordinance, such as non-payment of rent, owner move-in, demolition, or Ellis Act withdrawal. Merely ending a lease term or a change in ownership is not sufficient grounds for eviction.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to rental units covered by the San Francisco Rent Ordinance.
rules.quoted_span: In order to evict a tenant from a rental unit covered by the Rent Ordinance, a landlord must have a "just cause" reason that is the dominant motive for pursuing the eviction. Note that the mere expiration of a rental agreement or a change in ownership does not constitute "just cause" for eviction.

coverage.other_unknown_factor: whether the unit is covered by the Rent Ordinance

rules.title: San Francisco Relocation Assistance for No-Fault Evictions
rules.requirement: Landlords who evict tenants based on owner/relative move-in, demolition or permanent removal of a unit, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation must pay relocation assistance to displaced tenants, with additional amounts for elderly, disabled, or households with minor children.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to no-fault evictions under the Rent Ordinance based on owner/relative move-in, demolition/permanent removal, temporary capital improvement work, or substantial rehabilitation.
rules.quoted_span: Relocation Payments for Evictions based on Owner/Relative Move-in OR Demolition/Permanent Removal of Unit from Housing Use OR Temporary Capital Improvement Work* OR Substantial Rehabilitation
